Definition: from a primary ναίω (to dwell); a fane, shrine, temple:--shrine, temple. Compare G2411.
BiblicalUsage: Naos is the temple, the inner sanctuary where God dwells, and the New Testament uses it for a building, for a body, and for Christ Himself. In Matthew 23:16 Jesus rebukes the blind guides who swear by the temple and by its gold, and in John 2:19 He says, destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. In 1 Corinthians 3:16 believers are told they are the temple of God and the Spirit dwells in them, and in Revelation 11:1 John is told to measure the temple of God and the altar.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the temple is the place where God meets His people, and the wonder of the gospel is that the meeting place moved. It was a building, then it was a body raised in three days, and now it is the people in whom the Spirit dwells. I hold that my body is the temple now, and I should live like it.
